html:
Corsica is the mountainous island north of Sardinia, now part of France. On the map for 1000 to 1400 it is shown on its own, in the centuries when the Italian sea republics fought over it.

In 1077 the pope gave the bishop of Pisa authority over the island, and Pisa dominated it for two centuries, building Romanesque churches that still stand. Genoa contested it, and after Genoa smashed the Pisan fleet at the Battle of Meloria in 1284, the island passed into Genoese hands. The pope's grant of Sardinia and Corsica to Aragon in 1297 added a third claimant.

Genoa held on, against many revolts, for almost five hundred years. In 1755 Pasquale Paoli set up an independent Corsican republic with a written constitution. Genoa sold its rights to France in 1768, and France conquered the island the next year, the year Napoleon was born in Ajaccio.
sum: Corsica is the mountainous island north of Sardinia, now part of France. On the map for 1000 to 1400 it is shown on its own, in the centuries when the Italian sea republics fought over it.
